title: Stocks Slide Into a Correction. Hackers Hit Federal Systems. Bayer Settles Roundup Claims.
subject: Stocks Slide Into a Correction. Hackers Hit Federal Systems. Bayer Settles Roundup Claims.
preview_text: The S&P 500 falls 10% from its high, hackers hit two federal agencies, and Roundup claims get a payout plan.
description: Stocks enter a correction, hackers hit USDA and FBI systems, a child dies of measles in Virginia, and Bayer settles Roundup claims.
contents_extra: How a retrial ended with a guilty verdict in the Palisades Fire, trivia and your poll

stories.title: The S&P 500 and Dow Slide Into a Correction on a Rough Friday

photo.alt: Falling chart on a screen; file photo.

paragraphs: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday, the AP reports. That put it more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record, a level investors call a correction. The Nasdaq fell 5.3% and is now down for the year.

The Dow fell 1.9% and also entered a correction, CBS News reports. Chipmakers led losses on worries about slower data center building and tighter export rules. Wharton professor Jeremy Siegel told CNBC the drop resets expectations after three years of double-digit returns.

stories.title: Hackers Hit the Agriculture Department as the FBI Probes a Database Breach

photo.alt: Network switch with cables; file photo.

paragraphs: The Agriculture Department was hit by a cyberattack this week, according to two former USDA officials who spoke to NBC News. A system the agency uses to pay farmers was breached, officials said.

The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, two people briefed told NBC News. The system shares law enforcement information nationwide. The FBI had no comment as of Friday night, NBC reported.

stories.title: A Young Child Dies of Measles in Virginia, the State's First Death This Year

photo.alt: Gloved hand holding a syringe; file photo.

paragraphs: The Virginia Department of Health said a child aged 0 to 4 died after testing positive for measles. It is the state's first measles-associated death in 2026. The department cited a recent increase in measles activity.

ABC News reports it is the 12th measles-associated death reported by states this year. The CDC has logged 5,838 confirmed cases in 2026, ABC reports. Virginia officials say two MMR doses are about 97% effective.

stories.title: A Judge Approves Bayer's Roundup Cancer Settlement of Up to $7.25 Billion

photo.alt: Farmer spraying a green field; file photo.

paragraphs: Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion over two decades to settle claims that Roundup caused lymphoma, the AP reports. A St. Louis judge approved the deal Friday. Bayer denies that Roundup causes cancer.

Average payouts could range from $10,000 to $165,000, depending on use, age at diagnosis and severity, PBS reports, citing the AP. Some patient lawyers say the payouts are too small. Others say it beats getting nothing.

deep_dive.title: A Second Jury Convicts a Man of Starting the Palisades Fire

photo.alt: Hillside fire behind homes; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. A federal jury found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty of arson charges on Friday, the AP reports via PBS. His first trial ended in a mistrial in June, when jurors deadlocked 10 to 2 for acquittal. Prosecutors said he lit a fire on Jan. 1, 2025, that later flared into the Palisades Fire.

Why it matters. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people and destroyed over 6,000 homes and other structures, NBC News reports. It caused $25 billion in damage, a top federal prosecutor said. NBC calls it the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history. The verdict gives a legal answer on who started it.

What each side says. Prosecutors said phone location data placed him 30 feet from the fire, ABC News reports. They said he was angry and frustrated in the days before. Defense attorney Steve Haney cast doubt on the case, ABC reports. A defense expert argued the fire began somewhere else.

What comes next. Sentencing is set for March 17, NBC News reports. Rinderknecht faces a minimum of five years and up to 40 years in prison, prosecutors said. He was convicted on both federal counts, NBC reports. Those are destruction of property by fire and arson affecting interstate commerce.

World view: A strong quake rattles Peru. A magnitude 6.8 quake hit central Peru Friday, with no immediate reports of casualties or major damage; NBC News reports.
Denmark expels a Russian attache. Officials said they thwarted a plot, allegedly by Russian intelligence, to kill a Ukrainian American on Danish soil; NBC News reports.
Iraqi forces enter a militia stronghold. Troops deployed in Jurf al-Sakhar under a deal aimed at limiting Kataib Hezbollah's reach; NBC News reports.
A South African trailblazer dies. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, the first female deputy president and former UN Women chief, died at 71; NBC News reports.
Need to know: Trump limits contractor talks with Congress. A new order tells federal contractors to alert the White House before sharing information with lawmakers; CNBC reports.
A court faults a 2022 House vote. The 5th Circuit ruled 9-8 that the House unconstitutionally passed a $1.7 trillion bill using proxy votes; NBC News reports.
A court pauses an Iowa detonation. Judges temporarily blocked a permit for the Army to blow up nearly five tons of lead azide; ABC News reports.
Bed bugs close FEMA headquarters. Staff at the Washington building were told to work from home Friday, according to sources; ABC News reports.
Money & markets: Mailchimp gets a new owner. Bending Spoons is buying the email firm from Intuit for $3.68 billion, far below the $12 billion Intuit paid; TechCrunch reports.
Zscaler jumps on deal talk. Shares rose 18% after hours after Bloomberg reported CrowdStrike is in talks to buy the company; CNBC reports.
Nvidia drops 14% in a day. The chipmaker headed for a seventh straight weekly loss and is down 46% over that stretch; CNBC reports.
Kalshi faces a restraining order fight. New York's attorney general sought the order, and Kalshi warned it could cripple the platform; ABC News reports.
Future frontiers: A Dragon cargo ship heads home. The SpaceX capsule left the space station Friday and is due to splash down off California on Saturday; NASA says.
Talks on killer robots are pushed back. Countries agreed to keep working on rules within two years, a deal weakened by Russia's opposition; CNBC reports.
California subpoenas Nvidia. The state attorney general is investigating whether chips or secrets reached China, Bonta said; TechCrunch reports.
Protesters target Meta in India. Opposition youth activists clashed with police outside Meta offices over removed Instagram accounts; CNBC reports.
The score: Harden scores 51 for Cleveland. He passed Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games as the Cavaliers beat the Pacers 128-119; ESPN reports.
Drake Maye fractures his fibula. The Patriots quarterback is expected to miss much of the season, sources told ESPN; ESPN reports.
The Colts cut Daniel Jones. Indianapolis waived its quarterback a day after a 26-3 loss to Houston; ESPN reports.
The NWSL crowns a champion Saturday. The Kansas City Current, the only team with its own stadium, will face the Washington Spirit; CBS News reports.
Life & culture: Clothes cost more than they used to. Apparel prices have risen since the pandemic, and shoppers are focusing more on quality, research from AlixPartners says; CNBC reports.
New York's mayor tears his Achilles. Zohran Mamdani was hurt scoring a goal in a soccer match against the city press corps; NBC News reports.
A former Jackson mayor is sentenced. Chokwe Antar Lumumba got more than three years in prison in a bribery scheme; NBC News reports.
Watch for AI shopping scams. In a Norton survey, about 16% said they had been scammed shopping online during the holidays; CNBC reports.

trivia.question: How many people died in the 2025 Palisades Fire?
trivia.explanation: B. 12. The AP reports the Palisades Fire killed 12 people as it burned neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Malibu.
